raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Startup FlashInfer autotuning runs before the breakable prefill graph capture context. A model can select a different MoE path in graph mode: deferred finalize uses an `(N, 0)` output placeholder instead of the eager path's `(N, hidden_size)` output. These produce different tuning keys, so startup tuning can complete while the recorded prefill graph still uses a fallback tactic.

Tune the actual breakable prefill graph forward before recording its graphs. Related PR [#32556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32556) adds eager EXTEND warmup for larger token buckets; this change addresses the distinct tuning keys selected inside the BCG context.

Baseline: `a6b542813ff46de8ba3856e0236f1af35f4fca54`. Reviewed patch head: `6ad552c579`.

## Modifications

- In the existing breakable graph capture session, run FlashInfer autotuning using the largest configured prefill shape before recording capture buckets. The additional pass applies only to the breakable backend.
- Reuse `capture_prepare`, attention metadata preparation, and `_run_forward` so tuning follows the same model path as graph capture.
- Reuse the existing autotune eligibility check and context, including the disable/deterministic gates and configured skip operations. No new CLI flags or cache format changes.
- Exercise `capture()` with the real BCG capture session; the fake model selects its tuning key from the actual BCG context. Cover smaller buckets and disabled/deterministic modes. A separate boundary test verifies that Full and TC-piecewise only run their existing capture passes.

## Accuracy Tests

- Existing registered component test file: 11 tests passed. In-memory mutations restoring the upstream capture loop, removing the BCG context during tuning, or extending the new pass to all backends each fail the strengthened regression.
- Full-model bounded GSM8K regression: both baseline and patched scored **60/64 (93.75%)**, using the unchanged SGLang five-shot completion scorer, temperature 0, max tokens 512, and 8 threads.
- Four fixed greedy generation smoke cases produced identical text.

The 64-question evaluation is a sanity check; matching aggregate scores does not imply identical per-question outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Full `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (`aec724e8`), B200 TP4, FlashInfer 0.6.18, PyTorch 2.13.0, 2048-token prefill chunks, breakable prefill graphs, FP8 KV, prefix cache disabled. Official SGLang serving benchmark: 240 requests, 4096 input / 8 output tokens, concurrency 24, seed 42, temperature 0; separate 240-request warmup before measurement. The `random` dataset mode samples ShareGPT prompts and repeats or truncates their token IDs to exactly 4096 input tokens.

| Condition | Three run durations (s) | Median (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 44.770 / 44.873 / 44.889 | 44.873 |
| Patched | 42.414 / 42.503 / 42.647 | 42.503 |

Median workload duration decreased **5.28%**; input throughput increased **5.58%**. All six runs completed 240/240 requests with exactly 983,040 input and 1,920 output tokens and no request errors. These are unprofiled measurements, with three repeats within one warmed server instance per condition. Measurements preceded the final BCG-only eligibility restriction and test strengthening; the BCG forward and tuning sequence are unchanged.

Baseline used GPUs 4–7; patched used GPUs 0–3 on the same B200 host, with serialized benchmark load. GPU groups were not swapped. Both conditions independently generated their normal autotune caches; only compiled FlashInfer binaries were shared. Results apply to this prefill-heavy workload and deployment.

Persistent rank-0 cache evidence shows 20 eager / 0 graph MoE keys in baseline and 20 eager / 16 graph keys in patched. First graph-path tuning took approximately 91 seconds by logs; with cache reuse, it completed within the same logged second. Total initial startup times are confounded by compilation and checkpoint-cache state and are not compared as a patch effect.

Bounded Nsight Systems captures used the same node-level CUDA graph tracing and native NVTX switches, after the same warmup, for 24 requests of 4096 input / 8 output tokens at concurrency 24. Both traces contain 116,339 kernels per GPU, including 92,320 graph nodes. The selected prefill MoE boundary has exactly 75 layers × 48 chunks per GPU; decode graph nodes are present and excluded from this boundary.

| Prefill kernel metric, mean per call | Baseline (μs) | Patched (μs) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GEMM1 + GEMM2 interval union | 331.604 | 256.269 | 22.72% |
| Routing + GEMM1 + GEMM2 + finalize interval union | 386.667 | 314.115 | 18.76% |

The recorded GEMM1 tactic changes from `t128x32x512u2_s4` to `t128x128x512_s3x3x3x3x1x3`; GEMM2 changes from `t128x32x512_s5` to `t128x128x256_s6`. Interval unions account for overlapping kernels. This boundary excludes input quantization, shared-expert work, collectives, and subsequent fused operations. These profiled kernel measurements support the mechanism; they do not replace the unprofiled end-to-end score. Independent normal autotuning also selected different decode tactics, whose measured GEMM time was essentially unchanged; non-target tactics were not artificially synchronized.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction: pinned inputs, server, benchmark, and accuracy commands</summary>

These commands preserve the recorded arguments; machine-specific Python, model, dataset, cache, and output paths are replaced with portable paths. Use the baseline checkout at `a6b542813ff46de8ba3856e0236f1af35f4fca54` and the same checkout with this patch applied. Both use Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18, CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, and Transformers 5.12.1.

**Prepare the exact model and data once**, using the same absolute `REPRO_ROOT` for both conditions. This downloads the full model weights. The GSM8K conversion preserves the original row order; the evaluator uses the first five rows as demonstrations and evaluates the next 64.

```bash
export REPRO_ROOT="$PWD/glm52-autotune-repro"
mkdir -p "$REPRO_ROOT"
python - <<'PYDATA'
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shlex
from pathlib import Path

import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download, snapshot_download

root = Path(os.environ["REPRO_ROOT"]).resolve()
model = snapshot_download(
    "nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4",
    revision="aec724e8c7b8ee9db3b48c01c320f63f9cdaf8aa",
)
dataset = hf_hub_download(
    "anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered",
    "ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json",
    repo_type="dataset",
    revision="192ab2185289094fc556ec8ce5ce1e8e587154ca",
)
gsm8k_source = hf_hub_download(
    "openai/gsm8k",
    "main/test-00000-of-00001.parquet",
    repo_type="dataset",
    revision="740312add88f781978c0658806c59bc2815b9866",
)
for path, expected in [
    (dataset, "35f0e213ce091ed9b9af2a1f0755e9d39f9ccec34ab281cd4ca60d70f6479ba4"),
    (gsm8k_source, "ee7b8da9e381df27b9e3f7758a159ab2bdaa4dbaa910546cbbc47e0cb44e4f59"),
]:
    assert hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == expected

gsm8k = root / "gsm8k-test.jsonl"
with gsm8k.open("w") as output:
    for row in pq.read_table(gsm8k_source).to_pylist():
        output.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
with (root / "inputs.env").open("w") as output:
    for key, value in dict(REPRO_ROOT=str(root), MODEL=model,
                           DATASET=dataset, GSM8K=str(gsm8k)).items():
        output.write(f"export {key}={shlex.quote(value)}\n")
PYDATA
```

**Launch each condition from its own checkout**, with the prepared environment active. Set `REPRO_ROOT` to the preparation directory if using another terminal. Use `CASE=baseline` for the baseline, then `CASE=patched` for this patch. Run benchmark loads sequentially. The GPU assignments below match the measurements.

```bash
source "$REPRO_ROOT/inputs.env"
CASE=baseline  # Change to patched in the patched checkout.
case "$CASE" in
  baseline) export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7; PORT=30825 ;;
  patched)  export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3; PORT=30826 ;;
esac
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python"
export SGLANG_CACHE_DIR="$REPRO_ROOT/cache/$CASE"
export FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE="$REPRO_ROOT/cache/baseline"
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false TMPDIR=/tmp MAX_JOBS=16
mkdir -p "$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR" "$REPRO_ROOT/results/$CASE"

SERVER=(
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL" \
  --tp 4 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --context-length 131072 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT"
)
"${SERVER[@]}"
```

Keep this server running. In a client terminal, source `inputs.env`, set `CASE` and `PORT` to the running condition, and run from the same source checkout. Autotune caches are independent per condition; `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` shares compiled kernels only. The reported repeat runs reused caches populated by earlier startup; initial graph-path tuning costs are reported separately above.

```bash
source "$REPRO_ROOT/inputs.env"
CASE=baseline  # Change to patched for the patched server.
case "$CASE" in baseline) PORT=30825 ;; patched) PORT=30826 ;; esac
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
OUT="$REPRO_ROOT/results/$CASE"
mkdir -p "$OUT"

BENCH=(
python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --dataset-name random \
  --dataset-path "$DATASET" \
  --tokenize-prompt \
  --random-input-len 4096 \
  --random-output-len 8 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency 24 \
  --seed 42 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --warmup-requests 1 \
  --output-details
)
# After the server is ready: separate 240-request warmup, then three measurements.
"${BENCH[@]}" --num-prompts 240 --output-file "$OUT/warmup.jsonl"
for repeat in 1 2 3; do
  "${BENCH[@]}" --num-prompts 240 --output-file "$OUT/benchmark-$repeat.jsonl"
done

python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --eval-name gsm8k \
  --api completion \
  --num-examples 64 \
  --num-threads 8 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 512 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --gsm8k-data-path "$GSM8K"
```

`--dataset-name random` with the pinned ShareGPT file, `--tokenize-prompt`, and `--random-range-ratio 1.0` is the recorded benchmark configuration. Each invocation also retains the benchmark's one-request built-in warmup (`--warmup-requests 1`). Exclude the separate 240-request warmup from the three-run median. The correctness result for patched was collected in its first server instance; baseline accuracy was collected in its repeat-run instance, with identical server arguments and evaluator settings.

For the registered component test, run from the patched checkout:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py -v
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduction: separate Nsight Systems capture</summary>

Use a separate server launch for profiling, after completing the unprofiled measurements. With the same server setup and `SERVER` array above, launch through Nsight Systems with `nvtx==0.2.16` installed:

```bash
export SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_SCHEDULER=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS=1
nsys profile \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx \
  --cuda-graph-trace=node \
  --trace-fork-before-exec=true \
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \
  --capture-range-end=stop-shutdown \
  --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none \
  --force-overwrite=true --kill=none \
  -o "$REPRO_ROOT/results/$CASE/steady" \
  "${SERVER[@]}" --enable-layerwise-nvtx-marker
```

After readiness, run in the client terminal with the same `BENCH` array:

```bash
"${BENCH[@]}" --num-prompts 240 --output-file "$OUT/nsys-warmup.jsonl"
"${BENCH[@]}" --num-prompts 24 --output-file "$OUT/nsys-workload.jsonl" \
  --profile --profile-activities CUDA_PROFILER
```

The recorded launch also used a wrapper that saved the server PID before `exec`; it is omitted here because it does not change the server arguments or profiling configuration. Compare the prefill MoE graph nodes separately from decode nodes; the reported times use interval unions to avoid double-counting overlapping kernels. Do not use the profiled workload's throughput as the end-to-end performance result.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on commit `6ad552c579` in a clean temporary checkout, including Rust formatting and Clippy; no tracked files were modified.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Uses the existing CPU registration, `CustomTestCase`, real scoped config overrides, and the direct-file CI entry point; verified failing before the fix.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A for user documentation: no new configuration or usage interface. The cross-path tuning-key constraint is documented in code.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Provided a 64-question GSM8K sanity check and steady-state serving benchmarks (240 requests, concurrency 24, separate warmup, three repeats). GPU results cover the BCG implementation before the final backend-scope restriction; no new GPU evaluation was run on the final commit.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Separate BCG regression and backend-boundary tests; each new method is under 100 lines.

+class TestPrefillGraphAutotune(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        self.enterContext(get_parallel().override(tp_rank=1))
+        self.enterContext(
+            patch.object(runner_module, "get_available_gpu_memory", return_value=80)

+            model_config=SimpleNamespace(quantization=None),
+            spec_algorithm=SimpleNamespace(is_speculative=lambda: False),

+        runner._init_forward_metadata_for_capture = lambda *_args: None
+        runner.backend = BreakableCudaGraphBackend.__new__(BreakableCudaGraphBackend)
+        runner.backend._pool = (0, 0)
+        stream = object()
+        self.enterContext(
+            patch.object(runner_module, "freeze_gc", lambda *_a: nullcontext())

+        )
+
+    def test_bcg_records_graph_tactics_and_honors_opt_outs(self):
+        """Eager keys cannot tune deferred-finalize BCG calls, even at the same size."""
+        self._prepare_bcg_capture()
+        for policy in ("enabled", "disabled", "deterministic"):
+            with self.subTest(policy=policy):
+                tactics = {(8, 16): 7}
+                captured = {}
+                tuning_sizes = []
+                tuning = False
+
+                @contextmanager
+                def autotune_context(_mr, *, run_lm_head):
+                    nonlocal tuning
+                    self.assertFalse(run_lm_head)
+                    tuning = True
+                    try:
+                        yield
+                    finally:
+                        tuning = False
+
+                def forward(_batch, size):
+                    width = 0 if is_in_breakable_cuda_graph() else 16
+                    if tuning:
+                        tuning_sizes.append(size)
+                        for bucket in self.runner.capture_num_tokens:
+                            if bucket <= size:
+                                tactics[bucket, width] = 11
+                    return tactics.get((size, width), -1)
+
+                def capture_one(key, forward_fn, **_kwargs):
+                    self.assertFalse(tuning)
+                    self.assertTrue(is_in_breakable_cuda_graph())
+                    captured[key.size] = forward_fn()
+
+                self.runner._run_forward = forward
+                self.runner.backend.capture_one = capture_one
+                with (
+                    get_context().override_server_args(
+                        moe_runner_backend="flashinfer_trtllm",
+                        disable_flashinfer_autotune=policy == "disabled",
+                        enable_deterministic_inference=policy == "deterministic",
+                    ),
+                    patch.object(
+                        autotune_module, "flashinfer_autotune_context", autotune_context
+                    ),
+                ):
+                    self.runner.capture()
+                enabled = policy == "enabled"
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    captured, {8: 11, 4: 11} if enabled else {8: -1, 4: -1}
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(tuning_sizes, [8] if enabled else [])
+                self.assertFalse(is_in_breakable_cuda_graph())
+
+    def test_other_backends_only_record_capture_buckets(self):

+            get_context().override_server_args(

+                disable_flashinfer_autotune=False,
+                enable_deterministic_inference=False,
+            )

+        for backend_type in (FullCudaGraphBackend, TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend):
